questions.question_text: Miss Susie, a famous psephologist, constructs a Venn diagram to study the voting pattern among a sample population of 5000 voters. The survey requires the voter to identify election issues from among a list of five issues. A voter may identify none, one, or more than one of the issues listed as an election issue. How many distinct regions should the Venn diagram contain?
questions.solution_text: The Venn diagram has to describe 5 sets, say A, B, C, D, E.CBA Now, a point in a Venn diagram may belong to none, one or more of the five sets.127 136 Number of regions belonging to all 5 sets = 5C5145 Number of regions common to only 4 sets = 5C4235 Similarly, the number of regions common to 3, 2 and 1 sets is given by $^5C_3$, $5C_2$ and $^5C_1$. Also 5C0 gives the number of regions belonging to none of the sets. ∴ Total number of regions = $2^5$ = 32.
questions.full_markdown:
### Question 12
Miss Susie, a famous psephologist, constructs a Venn diagram ... How many distinct regions should the Venn diagram contain?
Solution: 32
